scale.1: 有问题（问题表里必须有对应条目）
scale.2: 基本没问题，有小瑕疵（写证据）

scoring.evidence_rule: 证据要指到句号 lNN / 屏号、原文或数字，至少 8 个字；没证据的高分按 0 处理。
scoring.disagreement: 分歧：两位同一维度差 ≥2，或一人 ≤1、另一人 ≥2，交裁决人；两人都 ≥2 的维度，裁决人每项抽 2 维复核（专抓两个模型共同的盲点）。

items.law_name: 中文口播（母语听感，盲审）
items.checks: 逐句听讲解员的中文：真人讲解会不会这么说、听一遍能不能懂。

items.problem: 上一版「本期内容」念成「这一期，讲四件事：它是个什么问题；为什么只背练习册不行……」，像在念目录，正常人不会这么说话（用户 2026-11-08 指出）；原先的审稿没抓到。
items.model_why: a 位 Claude、b 位 Codex 各自独立审；分歧与抽查交 Claude Opus 裁决

rubric.name: 像真人在讲
rubric.question: 逐句：自然 / 有点怪 / 很怪。书面腔、讲解腔、翻译腔、念稿感、报菜名式罗列都算怪

rubric.name: 衔接与过渡
rubric.question: 开场、本期内容、章节转换、举例前后：像一个人顺着思路往下讲，而不是「下面讲第一点」式的模板或目录朗读；上下句接得上

rubric.name: 一遍听懂
rubric.question: 只靠耳朵：一句只带一个新意思；指代清楚（说「这个」时观众知道指什么）；术语先解释再用；数字、同音字不会听错

rubric.name: 精炼
rubric.question: 没有废话、重复、正确的空话；删掉不影响理解的句子要指出来

rubric.name: 口吻与节奏
rubric.question: 从头到尾是同一个亲切、清楚、不端着的讲解者；长短句交替，每句适合一口气念完

rubric.name: 改写
rubric.question: 每句「有点怪 / 很怪」都给出可以直接替换、不更长的中文改写；列出最别扭的 5 句并排序

V1.evidence: 整体口语化好，如 l46「小孩会说「这不是数字」，它不会。」；但 l01 开场「能认出哪些照片里是你家的猫，可从来没人把猫长什么样，一条条写成规则教给它」、l37「这一期说的今天的 AI，就是机器学习这一圈」、l51「主要不靠人写规则，而是……」、l52「下一期讲过拟合：……」落在从严条目且有点怪。

V2.evidence: l38「从数据里学，也可能学歪。据路透社报道……」、l43「所以用 AI 的时候，记住三点」接得顺；小瑕疵在 l27「换个角度，今天的 AI 像一台预测机器」转得硬，l37 章节收束带「说的今天的」堆叠。

V3.evidence: l45「有百分之九十二的把握是四。这个把握，只是在十个数字里比谁更像」术语落地清楚；但 l17「一共一千七百九十七张」、l23-l24 连报「百分之三十七 / 十 / 八十八 / 九十七」数字密，l41 一句塞英文词、中文释义、例子三层。

V4.evidence: l19「训练时考试题一张都不许看」与 l18「锁起来当考试题」、画面「训练时不许看」重复；l12「其实大多是从例子里学来的」与 l08-l10 重复，但 l12 要引出「数据」一词，可保留。

V5.evidence: 全程亲切、不端着，「咱们真做一次」「待会儿就能看到」是一个人在讲；节奏小问题：l01(7.9s)、l05(9.4s)、l12(8.9s)、l17(8.8s)偏长一口气，l35「由很多层简单的计算叠起来」突然书面。

V6.evidence: 下方问题表对每个「有点怪」都给了不更长的替换句；最别扭 5 句排序见整体观察。

V1.evidence: 52 个口播条目中，33 条自然，17 条有点怪，2 条很怪。l37“这一期说的今天的 AI”修饰语打结；l45“这个把握，只是在十个数字里比谁更像”主语和后半句接不上。

V2.evidence: l27“换个角度，今天的 AI 像一台预测机器”突然换一套说法；l33“刚才这些词，是一圈套一圈的”没有说清在串哪几个词；l52“下一期讲过拟合”先报题目，再补问题，像念片尾提纲。

V3.evidence: l15“你指的数字加上‘这是三’”要在脑中重新组合才能理解；l23“这样抽二十回，成绩一般只有百分之三十七左右”没有明确每回还要学习、考试；l45“这个把握”具体表示什么，一遍听不清。

V4.evidence: l12“很多人以为，AI 的本事是程序员一条条写进去的”重复前面已经讲清的区别，只保留“这些例子就叫数据”也能衔接；l17“一千七百九十七张”之后紧跟“八行八列的小格子”，增加了暂时用不上的记忆负担。

V5.evidence: l21“你先猜猜：只给它看十个例子”亲切自然，但 l33 转成概念分类，l47 又用“它给的是预测，不是真理”喊总结口号，口吻不够一致；l17 标注 8.8 秒，同时塞入开实验、数据来源、总数和图片规格，节奏偏赶。

items.problem: The previous agenda read 'In this episode: What the problem is. Why memorizing answers fails. A different way to think about learning…' — a table of contents read aloud. No one talks like that (caught by the user, 2026-11-08); earlier reviews missed it.

rubric.name: Sounds like a person talking
rubric.question: Each line: natural / a bit off / clearly off. Written-style, lecture tone, translated-from-Chinese phrasing, telegraphic lists all count as off

rubric.name: Flow and transitions
rubric.question: Cold open, the 'what's coming' part, chapter changes, before/after examples: does it sound like one person following a thought, not 'Point one…' templates or a TOC read aloud? Do adjacent lines connect?

rubric.name: Clear on one hearing
rubric.question: Ear only: one new idea per line; clear reference ('this' points to something); terms explained before used; numbers and words not misheard

rubric.name: Tight
rubric.question: No filler, repetition, or empty truisms; point out lines that could go without losing anything

rubric.name: Voice and rhythm
rubric.question: One warm, clear, unpretentious narrator throughout; varied sentence length; each line sayable in one breath

rubric.name: Rewrites
rubric.question: For every 'a bit off' / 'clearly off' line, a drop-in rewrite no longer than the original; rank the 5 most awkward lines

V1.evidence: most lines sound spoken ("Now try writing down how.", "take a guess", "A kid would say, 'That's not a number.'"); off spots are l52 "Next time: overfitting, or why…", l32 "sounding smooth doesn't guarantee being right", l35 "made of many layers of simple calculations".

V2.evidence: cold open l01→l02 ("So how does it do it?") and the digit story l05→l07 flow like one person thinking; but l43–l48 "One: / Two: / Three:" reads as a numbered template, and l52 is a headline-plus-"or why" outro.

V3.evidence: one idea per line mostly holds, "Fat, skinny, tilted" lands instantly; but l17 "seventeen ninety-seven" sounds like a year, l26 "like this messy two" and l28 "this one's a three" point at visuals an ear cannot see, l23 "Do that twenty times" has a fuzzy referent.

V4.evidence: l16 "a model needs way more examples, as you'll see" and l19+l20 (training/never sees test, then "only unseen questions can show…") repeat each other; l12 "Mostly, it learned from examples" repeats l08–l10.

V5.evidence: one warm narrator throughout, good short/long mix (l46 "The model won't." vs l30); l35 (9.2s, two ideas + a term) and l33 are not one-breath lines.

V6.evidence: every off line below has a drop-in rewrite no longer than the original; top five ranked in 整体观察.

V1.evidence: l15 reads like an equation spoken aloud; l44 “answer even things it never learned” and l50 “learned this kind of question” are awkward English collocations.

V2.evidence: l01–l02 make a clear, conversational opening. However, l33 introduces an abstract taxonomy abruptly, while l51 “In a sentence” and l52 “Next time: overfitting, or why…” bring back a scripted outline voice.

V3.evidence: l17 “seventeen ninety-seven” initially sounds like a year. l23 leaves the repeated procedure unclear, and l35 introduces several nested categories and a new technical term in one turn.

V4.evidence: The experiment and Amazon example earn their space. Smaller repetitions remain: l12 restates learning from examples after l10–l11, and l32 repeats that idea before reaching its useful warning.

V5.evidence: l06 “Now try writing down how” and l47 “That messy two?” have good spoken rhythm. l15’s equation-like construction and l35’s compressed definitions interrupt that otherwise approachable voice. Actual delivery cannot be assessed from text.

V6.evidence: Every line marked “a bit off” or “clearly off” below has a drop-in rewrite no longer than its original. The five most awkward lines are ranked under 整体观察.

Counting rules (round-2 ruling, 2026-11-09): eyebrow labels, case tabs, source lines and end-card credits are exempt; a list, table or card row of look-alike items (each ≤6 words, at most 6 items) counts as one block, and numbering doesn't count as words; in-chart text (zone names, curve names, axis titles, bar labels, callouts) counts toward words and the whole chart counts as one block — only axis tick numbers are exempt; a table's column headers count with the table.

rubric.name: Outline, not prose
rubric.question: Only keywords, short phrases, key numbers, labels; no full narration sentences. Count words per screen against the hard limits

rubric.name: Divided from narration
rubric.question: Screen carries structure, numbers, contrasts; narration explains. No verbatim repetition, no new claims the narration doesn't make; terms match the narration

rubric.name: Hierarchy and consistency
rubric.question: What reads first, second; ≤3 levels (title, point, note); numbering, labels, chapter names and agenda items consistent with each other

rubric.name: Native phrasing and style
